title: PTNK 2026 · Tiếng Anh Không chuyên
subtitle: Đề thi tuyển sinh lớp 10 · Trường Phổ thông Năng khiếu · 2026-2027

questions.q: Choose the word whose underlined part pronounces differently from the other three.
questions.explanation: "façade" /fəˈsɑːd/ has the /s/ sound; locale /ləʊˈkɑːl/, choir /kwaɪə/ and mechanic /məˈkænɪk/ all have /k/.

questions.q: Choose the word whose underlined part pronounces differently from the other three.
questions.explanation: In "experiment" /ɪkˈsperɪmənt/ the unstressed prefix is /ɪks/; in execute, extrovert and excavate the stressed first syllable is /eks/.

questions.q: Choose the word whose primary stress position differs from the other three.
questions.explanation: advan-TA-geous is stressed on the third syllable; con-DI-tioner, ap-PREN-ticeship and un-PLEA-santness on the second.

questions.q: Choose the word whose primary stress position differs from the other three.
questions.explanation: pre-SERVE is stressed on the second syllable; VA-cuum, VE-hicle and BO-ther on the first.

questions.q:
Rumi: 'Sorry, I couldn't make it to your slumber party because my sister wouldn't give me a ride.'
Mira: '______! There was a power cut at my place and it was so hot.'
Rumi: 'Oh, really?'
questions.explanation: Mira tells Rumi she missed nothing good — there was a power cut and it was hot — so "Consider yourself lucky" (you were fortunate not to come) is the natural reply.

questions.q: Since this test does not count toward the final score, nobody is going to revise, ______?
questions.explanation: "nobody" is negative and takes the pronoun "they" in a question tag, and the verb is the auxiliary of "is going to": nobody is going to revise, are they?

questions.q: Since his father passed away in an accident, Tiến is raised by his mother in a(n) ______ family.
questions.explanation: A child brought up by only one parent lives in a single-parent family.

questions.q: My teacher is so strict! If you ______ move during his exam, you will receive a penalty.
questions.explanation: "so much as" (= even) emphasises that the smallest action counts: if you so much as move, you will be penalised.

questions.q: Thương has a 9-step skincare regimen that she considers part of her nightly ______ before bed.
questions.explanation: A personal routine done the same way every night is a "nightly ritual"; tradition, custom and ceremony describe shared or formal practices.

questions.q: According to my timing, Kim ______ in 2 minutes, so everyone get in position now for the surprise!
questions.explanation: "should + verb" expresses a confident expectation based on evidence ("according to my timing"): Kim should arrive in 2 minutes.

questions.q: Before you join our team, we need to know if you are committed ______ the project your 100% effort.
questions.explanation: "be committed to + V-ing": the "to" is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund.

questions.q: Laughing at Mario, Bowser said "You're too slow. When you get to the castle, my minions ______ the Princess away!"
questions.explanation: The future perfect describes an action completed before a future time point ("when you get to the castle"): they will have taken her away by then.

questions.q: Either Jim or his children ______ the parcel at the post office today.
questions.explanation: With "either … or" the verb agrees with the nearer subject ("his children" → have), and collecting a parcel is "pick up", not "come across" (find by chance).

questions.q: Once you finish the last test item, it is good practice to ______ the answers at least once before submitting.
questions.explanation: "go over" = check or review carefully; "brush up on" is to improve rusty knowledge and "look back on" is to remember the past.

questions.q: The presentation ______ I am preparing is very important.
questions.explanation: "prepare for something" → "the presentation for which I am preparing"; a preposition cannot precede "that" in a relative clause.

questions.q: (A) Being fined 10 million VND once (B) for drinking and driving, Khoa promises to (C) himself (D) to never visit a bar with his friends again.
questions.explanation: The fine happened once in the past, before the present promise, so the perfect participle is needed: "Having been fined 10 million VND once …".

questions.q: Timmy lives so (A) far away from school (B) that (C) his coming to class (D) lately has become an everyday occurrence.
questions.explanation: "lately" means recently; the intended meaning is "not on time", which is the adverb "late": his coming to class late.

questions.q: Many changes (A) were occurred in the city between 2010 (B) and 2020, particularly in the financial district, (C) which saw the construction of multiple (D) high-rises.
questions.explanation: "occur" is intransitive and has no passive form: many changes occurred.

questions.q: Hardly (A) had George spent time (B) with his family (C) than the boss requested him (D) to fly back to the New York office.
questions.explanation: The pattern is "Hardly … when" ("No sooner … than"): Hardly had George spent time with his family when the boss requested him to fly back.

questions.q: (A) As a parent, you ought (B) to know that it does not teach good behaviour to always have somebody else (C) to clean up (D) after your son.
questions.explanation: Causative "have somebody do something" takes the bare infinitive: have somebody else clean up after your son.

questions.passage:
If you think of the jobs robots could never do, you would probably put doctors and teachers at the top of the list. It's easy to imagine robot cleaners and factory workers, but some jobs need human connection and creativity. Are we underestimating what robots can do? In some cases, they already perform better than doctors at diagnosing illness. Also, some patients might feel more comfortable sharing personal information with a machine than a person. Could there be a place for robots in education after all?

British education expert Anthony Seldon thinks so. He even has a date for the robot takeover of the classroom: 2027. He predicts robots will do the main job of transferring information and teachers will be like assistants. Intelligent robots will read students' faces, movements and maybe even brain signals. Then they will adapt the information to each student. It's not a popular opinion and it may be a challenge for robots to have empathy and the ability to really connect with humans like another human can.

One thing is certain, though. A robot teacher is better than no teacher at all. In some parts of the world, there aren't enough teachers and 9–16 per cent of children under the age of 14 don't go to school. That problem could be partly solved by robots because they can teach anywhere and won't get stressed, or tired, or move somewhere for an easier, higher-paid job.

Those negative aspects of teaching are something everyone agrees on. Teachers all over the world are leaving because it is a difficult job and they feel overworked. [I] Perhaps the question is not 'Will robots replace teachers?' but 'How can robots help teachers?' Office workers can use software to do things like organise and answer emails, arrange meetings with clients, and update calendars. [II] Teachers waste a lot of time doing non-teaching work, including more than 11 hours a week marking homework. [III] If robots could cut the time teachers spend marking homework and writing reports, teachers would have more time and energy for the parts of the job humans do best. [IV]
questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Why experts believe human teachers will be completely replaced by 2027
The reasons why teachers all over the world are leaving their profession
Robots being already more efficient than human doctors and teachers
The potential benefits of integrating robots into the field of education
questions.explanation: The whole passage explores "a place for robots in education" — as teachers where there are none, and as helpers that free teachers from non-teaching work.

options: They feel certain because robots don't get tired or stressed during the session.
They are diagnosed at much higher accuracy compared to human doctors.
They are more easily connected with robot doctors on an emotional level.
They feel more relaxed when they share personal details with a machine.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1: "some patients might feel more comfortable sharing personal information with a machine than a person".

questions.passage:
Whether you're travelling to the islands or the mountains of Thailand, you're likely to spend at least one night in its capital city on the way. Bangkok might be noisy and (29)____ but it's also an exciting city with plenty of things to see and do. Why not make it a longer stay?

Where to stay
The Khao San Road was a famous traveller spot even before Leonardo di Caprio's character in the film The Beach stayed there, but it's noisy, not very pretty and not very Thai. For something more (30)____, Phra Kanong offers an alternative place to stay, with its fantastic street markets where everyday Bangkok people eat, work and live. It's not as convenient for the main tourist sites, but it has a Skytrain station so you can be at the Grand Palace in 20 minutes.

How to get around
Bangkok's traffic can be a nightmare. Sure, you can easily take a taxi – if you want to spend hours stuck in traffic jams – but there are two much better ways to get around the city. To explore the temples and historical sites, (31)____ an express boat river taxi or a longtail boat along the Chao Phraya river and the canals. For the modern part of the city, the Skytrain is a fast, cheap way to travel from the river to the shopping malls and nightlife of Sukhumvit, and the famous Chatuchak street market.

Where to eat
The simple answer is: everywhere! Thai street food is among the best in the world, and for around $5 you can eat a filling and delicious meal. Some food stands have little plastic seats where you can sit and eat and they cook the same dish over and over, like fried chicken on rice or Pad Thai noodles. Head for Chinatown – Yaowarat Street – and choose (32)____ looks most interesting from the many excellent Chinese and Thai restaurants and food stands.

What to do
After you've seen the main sites like the Giant Buddha at the temple of Wat Pho and the spectacular Grand Palace, and shopped at Chatuchak market, check out the snake farm and watch the live snake show. You can even touch a snake yourself if you want to!
questions.explanation: The blank pairs with "noisy" as a drawback contrasted by "but it's also an exciting city": noisy and polluted.

Where to stay
The Khao San Road was a famous traveller spot even before Leonardo di Caprio's character in the film The Beach stayed there, but it's noisy, not very pretty and not very Thai. For something more (30)____, Phra Kanong offers an alternative place to stay, with its fantastic street markets where everyday Bangkok people eat, work and live. It's not as convenient for the main tourist sites, but it has a Skytrain station so you can be at the Grand Palace in 20 minutes.

How to get around
Bangkok's traffic can be a nightmare. Sure, you can easily take a taxi – if you want to spend hours stuck in traffic jams – but there are two much better ways to get around the city. To explore the temples and historical sites, (31)____ an express boat river taxi or a longtail boat along the Chao Phraya river and the canals. For the modern part of the city, the Skytrain is a fast, cheap way to travel from the river to the shopping malls and nightlife of Sukhumvit, and the famous Chatuchak street market.

Where to eat
The simple answer is: everywhere! Thai street food is among the best in the world, and for around $5 you can eat a filling and delicious meal. Some food stands have little plastic seats where you can sit and eat and they cook the same dish over and over, like fried chicken on rice or Pad Thai noodles. Head for Chinatown – Yaowarat Street – and choose (32)____ looks most interesting from the many excellent Chinese and Thai restaurants and food stands.

What to do
After you've seen the main sites like the Giant Buddha at the temple of Wat Pho and the spectacular Grand Palace, and shopped at Chatuchak market, check out the snake farm and watch the live snake show. You can even touch a snake yourself if you want to!
questions.q: What is the most suitable title for the text?
options: A Comprehensive Itinerary for a Long Stay in Bangkok
Discovering the Authentic and Modern Faces of Bangkok
A Survivor's Guide to Bangkok's Traffic and Cuisine
Uncovering Khao San Road: The Heart of Thai Culture
questions.explanation: The text pairs the genuinely local (Phra Kanong markets, street food, temples) with the modern (Skytrain, Sukhumvit malls and nightlife); it is a short overview, not a full itinerary, and Khao San Road is dismissed as "not very Thai".

questions.q: What is implied about Bangkok's transportation system?
options: Taxis are among the easiest methods for tourists to get to historical sites quickly.
The Skytrain is exclusively designed to connect the Chao Phraya river to Chatuchak.
Motorized road vehicles are the best way to experience the lively nightlife of the city.
Water-based transport is considered one of the strategic solutions to road congestion.
questions.explanation: Taxis mean "hours stuck in traffic jams", and one of the "two much better ways" offered is the express boat or longtail boat along the river and canals.

questions.q: According to the text, what is NOT TRUE about dining and activities in Bangkok?
options: Street food is a budget-friendly option, with satisfying meals costing around $5.
Yaowarat Street is a prime location to sample both Chinese and Thai cuisine.
Visitors can watch the live snake show but not come in contact with the animals.
Some food stands are highly specialized in cooking specific dishes like Pad Thai.
questions.explanation: The last line says the opposite: "You can even touch a snake yourself if you want to!"

questions.q: His ______ led to several mistakes in the final report. (COMPETENT)
questions.explanation: A noun is needed after "His", and the sense is negative (it caused mistakes): incompetence.

questions.q: Affordable housing schemes are devised to tackle the issue of ______ in urban areas. (HOME)
questions.explanation: "the issue of + noun": the problem that affordable housing solves is homelessness.

questions.q: She is a very ______ writer who can create entire worlds filled with mythical creatures. (IMAGINE)
questions.explanation: An adjective describing a person with a lot of imagination: an imaginative writer.

questions.q: To be a successful leader, you must be able to handle stressful situations ______. (EFFECT)
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb "handle": handle situations effectively.

questions.q: Using audio guides and virtual maps, visitors can take a ______ tour of the castle. (GUIDE)
questions.explanation: An adjective before "tour". "Using audio guides and virtual maps" means visitors tour the castle without a human guide, so the intended word is "self-guided" (a self-guided tour); the plain "guided tour" is grammatical but weaker, since a guided tour is normally led by a guide.

questions.q: Even though we are not her friends, we are ______ to the struggles she is facing. (SYMPATHY)
questions.explanation: "be sympathetic to/towards something" — the adjective is needed after "are".

questions.q: Many ______ are working together to study the effects of climate change. (ECOLOGY)
questions.explanation: A plural noun for people after "Many" and before "are working": ecologists (scientists who study ecology).

questions.q: Many Vietnamese people have the habit of riding motorbikes on the ______ although it is illegal. (WALK)
questions.explanation: A noun for the path beside the road that pedestrians use: the sidewalk (British "pavement").

questions.q:
If there are any questions, please contact us by email. (SEND)
→ Should ______ email.
accept: you have any questions, please send us an
you have any questions please send us an
you have any questions, send us an
you have any questions send us an
you have any questions, please send an
you have any question, please send us an
there be any questions, please send us an
there be any questions, send us an
there be any questions send us an
questions.answer: you have any questions, please send us an
questions.explanation: Inverted first conditional "Should you have …" (= If you have …); "contact us by email" becomes "send us an email".

questions.q:
It was a mistake for you to go out in the rain without an umbrella. (SHOULD)
→ You ______ in the rain without an umbrella.
questions.explanation: "should not have + past participle" criticises a past action that was a mistake: you shouldn't have gone out.

questions.q:
We are thinking of appointing Như to the position of Student Body President. (CONSIDERED)
→ Như ______ the position of Student Body President.
accept: is being considered by us for
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive of "consider somebody for a position": Như is being considered for the position.

questions.q:
People think that the ancient temple was destroyed by a natural disaster. (THOUGHT)
→ The ancient temple ______ by a natural disaster.
accept: is thought to have been destroyed
questions.answer: is thought to have been destroyed
questions.explanation: Impersonal passive with a perfect infinitive for an earlier action: "is thought to have been destroyed" (= people think it was destroyed).

questions.q:
"Don't forget to check the subway schedule before you leave," my mother said. (REMINDED)
→ My mother ______ before I left.
accept: reminded me to check the subway schedule
reminded me to check the subway schedules
reminded me to check the subway timetable
reminded me not to forget to check the subway schedule
questions.answer: reminded me to check the subway schedule
questions.explanation: Reported speech: "Don't forget to do something" → "remind somebody to do something"; "you leave" shifts to "I left".

questions.q:
If people have more awareness of environmental issues, they will act more responsibly towards the planet. (THE)
→ ______ are, the more responsibly they will act.
accept: The more aware of environmental issues people
The more aware of environmental issues that people
The more environmentally aware that people
questions.explanation: Double comparative "the more …, the more …": "have more awareness of environmental issues" becomes "the more environmentally aware people are".

questions.q:
It was a serious moment, but I couldn't stop myself from laughing. (HELP)
→ I couldn't ______ it was a serious moment.
questions.explanation: "can't help + V-ing" (or "can't help but + bare infinitive") = can't stop oneself; the contrast "but" becomes "even though/although".
